title: canary-sociotechnical-checklist-and-ops-scratchpad
content:
Summary:
This scratchpad captures a sociotechnical canary checklist and lightweight operations choreography for cross-functional rollouts and A/B experiments. Focus is on the human rituals that must accompany signal thresholds, plus practical heuristics for short, observable canaries when a new model variant or routing policy is introduced.

Purpose:
- Reduce mismatch between telemetry signals and human decision-making during early exposure.
- Give an ops-light, repeatable path teams can adopt for low-risk canaries and small A/Bs.
- Surface non-technical failure modes (communication gaps, steward fatigue, misaligned incentives).

Scope:
- Intended for product + SRE + research + solutions-eng working cross-functionally.
- Applies to: model variant rollouts, fallback policy changes, routing weight shifts, quantization profile swaps.
- Not for infra-scale network or datacenter-level incidents (SRE runbooks remain primary).

Key definitions (working):
- Sociotechnical canary: a short, instrumented exposure that couples technical thresholds with explicit human rituals (steward, observer, comms path).
- Steward: the named owner (1–2 ppl) who runs the activation, has commit rights to revert traffic, and drives post-mortem.
- Observer: cross-team person(s) focused only on signals and escalation, not making product-judgement calls.
- Signal escrow: a pre-configured set of fallback actions (model fallback, traffic split, emergency kill-switch) encoded in the console and reviewed pre-launch.

Run phases and minimum artifacts (checklist):
1) Pre-flight (T - 48 to T - 2 hours)
   - Quick stakeholder sync (5–10m): steward + observers + oncall rep. Confirm hypothesis and rollback criteria.
   - Confirm experiment manifest in Console: model ids, weights, routes, telemetry tags. Link PR/commit.
   - Create short-lived experiment channel (Slack thread) and add stakeholder ping list.
   - Verify telemetry dashboard template exists (latency tail, p95/p99, cost per token, quality deltas on golden prompts).
   - Smoke test in staging with synthetic traffic; record base-line traces.

2) Activation (T0 to T0 + 30m)
   - Start at micro-exposure: 0.1% traffic or 1 rpm for internal cohorts.
   - Steward posts activation note with timestamp, expected observation window, and primary signals to watch.
   - Observers confirm dashboards ingesting traffic and KV caches warming (if applicable).
   - Run quick sanity eval on a short prompt set (10–20 golden prompts) and post results.

3) Pulse-check cadence (T + 30m to T + 6h)
   - 0–30m: check minute-level runtime metrics for OOMs, error spikes, NACKs.
   - 30–90m: check latency p95/p99 trends and early quality regressions on golden prompts.
   - 3–6h: observe cost-per-token and model-side queueing behavior; validate no user-visible regressions.
   - At each pulse, steward marks PASS / WARN / FAIL and records short rationale in channel.

4) Escalation & rollback decision heuristic (one-line rule):
   - Fail if any of: sustained error-rate increase > 2x baseline for 15m, latency p99 increase > 200ms sustained for 30m causing downstream SLAs to fail, or quality regression on golden prompt set crossing defined error budget.
   - WARN when small anomalies observed (single-component spike, flakey downstream dependency) — increase visibility and postpone weight increases.
   - If fail -> immediate rollback to pre-configured signal escrow and page oncall.

Signals (minimum canonical set):
- System: request error rate (5xx), NACKs, OOM counts, host CPU/GPU saturation, queue length.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99, tail correlation with batch size and seq length.
- Cost: token/sec, GPU utilization per request type, pre/post-quantization delta.
- Quality: eval pass-rate on golden set, hallucination indicator (heuristic), rerank score delta.
- User-facing: logical correctness regressions, throughput drops for key customers.

Sociotechnical additions (what to actually say/do):
- Steward activation script (copy-paste):
   "Activating canary: variant=v2-quant, weight=0.1%. Window=3h. Observers=@ethan,@priya. Watchlist: p99 latency, 5xx, golden-evals. If FAIL -> rollback variant -> notify #ops-announce."
- Observer confirmation script: one-liner templated responses for each pulse.

Steward rota & small-batch handoff (practical):
- Prefer 2-person stewardship: primary + secondary. Primary monitors the first 60–90m; secondary takes longer horizon and runs follow-ups.
- Rotation window = 6–12h for active stewarding. Use calendar blocks and Slack reminders.
- Handoff note template (to be posted when passing from primary to secondary): timestamp, last-pulse state, outstanding concerns, next-check time.

Experiment design heuristics to avoid 'silent drift':
- Include a fixed golden prompt set that is run automatically against both control and variant every 15–60m during exposure.
- Surface lexical/semantic drift metrics (e.g., token overlap, hallucination heuristics) not just aggregate scores.
- Avoid mixing many changes in one canary (no more than one major model change + one routing tweak).

Comms and psychological safety guidance:
- Use "we revert first, investigate second" rule for user-visible failures. Prioritize containment.
- Automate immediate short messages (on fail) with action verbs (rollback called, who paged, what known symptoms).
- Post-mortems should be blameless and emphasize decision-process rather than person-level error.

Edge cases and anti-patterns we saw in past runs (field notes):
- Anti-pattern: pushing weight increases automatically after first PASS without human confirmation; leads to oscillation.
- Anti-pattern: too-large group of observers with no clear steward -> delay in decisions.
- Edge: caching warm-up causing transient errors misinterpreted as model regressions; use short traffic ramp with cache warmers.

Quick templates (copyable):
- Activation message: see steward activation script above.
- Rollback message: "Rollback executed at <TS> by <steward>. Reason: <short reason>. Traffic restored to <variant>. Oncall paged: <id>. Postmortem link: <placeholder>."

Open questions (to resolve before we standardize):
- Should the Console enforce a minimum "activation window" (e.g., 3h) for canaries to prevent flapping? Pros/cons.
- How to encode golden prompt sets per product (ownership, storage, and updates)?
- Is the 0.1% micro-exposure adequate for high-traffic rerankers where sample variance is tiny? Require variant-specific guidance.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with SRE on automated page rules for model-side OOM vs infra OOM (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Prototype a stewarding checkbox in Console that wires to Slack thread templates (owner: Jonah).
- [ ] Draft a short "canary etiquette" one-pager for PMs and SEs (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Gather 3 historical canary incidents, extract decision points for postmortem playbook (owner: Marina).

References and links: linked_artifacts above. Also see: confluence:CONS-3142-canary-ontology for signal definitions and ENG-7894 for previous rollout incident discussion.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally chatty and lightweight — the goal is a practical checklist teams will actually follow. Capture more examples from team retros.

-- end of scratchpad --
